questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is inflation?

options.A: A one-time rise in the price of a single commodity
options.B: A sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services over time
options.C: A fall in the general price level over time
options.D: A rise in the value of money

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services over time, reducing the purchasing power of money. A rise in one item alone is not necessarily general inflation.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What does CPI measure?

options.A: Price changes at the wholesale/producer level
options.B: Changes in prices paid by households for a representative basket of goods and services
options.C: Changes in the value of exports

questions.explanation: Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures changes in prices paid by households for a representative basket of goods and services.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which institution publishes CPI in India?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: In India, MoSPI/NSO publishes CPI. CPI inflation is widely used for monetary-policy targeting.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which institution publishes WPI?

options.A: MoSPI/NSO

questions.explanation: WPI is published by the Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is true about WPI?

options.A: It is a direct measure of household retail cost of living
options.B: It measures price changes at the wholesale/producer level for a selected basket
options.D: It is used for monetary-policy targeting

questions.explanation: WPI measures price changes at the wholesale/producer level for a selected basket. It is not a direct measure of household retail cost of living.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is core inflation?

options.A: Inflation in food prices only
options.B: A commonly used analytical measure excluding volatile food and fuel components
options.D: Inflation measured at the wholesale level

questions.explanation: Core inflation is a commonly used analytical measure excluding volatile food and fuel components. The precise definition must be checked in the relevant publication.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Demand-pull inflation occurs when:

options.A: Input costs such as fuel and wages rise
options.B: Aggregate demand rises faster than productive capacity
options.C: Expectations and wage-price adjustments sustain price increases
options.D: Depreciation raises the domestic cost of imports

questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand rises faster than productive capacity.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Cost-push inflation is caused by:

options.A: Aggregate demand rising faster than capacity
options.B: Rise in input costs such as fuel, wages, transport or imported raw materials
options.D: A fall in the general price level

questions.explanation: Cost-push inflation occurs when input costs such as fuel, wages, transport or imported raw materials rise.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Built-in inflation is sustained by:

options.A: A one-time rise in input costs
options.D: A rise in the value of the currency

questions.explanation: Built-in inflation is sustained by expectations and wage-price adjustments.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Imported inflation occurs when:

options.A: Aggregate demand rises faster than capacity
options.B: Depreciation or higher world prices raises the domestic cost of imports

questions.explanation: Imported inflation occurs when depreciation or higher world prices raise the domestic cost of imports.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is disinflation?

options.A: A fall in the general price level
options.B: A slowdown in the rate of inflation
options.C: A rise in the general price level
options.D: A rise in the value of money

questions.explanation: Disinflation means the inflation rate slows. Deflation means the general price level falls.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is deflation?

options.A: A slowdown in the rate of inflation
options.B: A fall in the general price level
options.C: A rise in the general price level
options.D: A rise in the value of money

questions.explanation: Deflation means the general price level falls.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Under the RBI's flexible inflation-targeting framework, what is the CPI target?

options.A: 2% with a tolerance band of 1%-3%

questions.explanation: The RBI's flexible inflation-targeting framework uses a 4% CPI target with a tolerance band of 2%-6%.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Who sets the inflation target under the flexible inflation-targeting framework?

options.A: RBI alone
options.B: The Central Government in consultation with RBI for a five-year period

questions.explanation: The target is set by the Central Government in consultation with RBI for a five-year period. The MPC decides the policy rate to achieve the target.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which body decides the policy rate to achieve the inflation target?

options.A: Central Government
options.B: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI

questions.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decides the policy rate to achieve the target.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is GDP?

options.A: The market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory during a specified period
options.B: The value of final goods and services produced within a State's economic territory
options.C: The total income of residents from abroad
options.D: The value of exports minus imports

questions.explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory during a specified period.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is GSDP?

options.A: The value of final goods and services produced within a State's economic territory
options.B: The market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory
options.C: The total expenditure of the State Government
options.D: The total tax revenue of the State

questions.explanation: Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) is the state-level counterpart of GDP: the value of final goods and services produced within a State's economic territory.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the GDP expenditure identity?

options.A: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M)
options.C: GDP = C + I + G + X + M

questions.explanation: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M), where C is private consumption, I is investment, G is government final consumption and X-M is net exports.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is nominal GDP?

options.A: GDP measured at constant prices

questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices. Real GDP is measured at constant prices to remove the effect of price changes.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is real GDP?

options.A: GDP measured at current prices
options.B: GDP measured at constant prices to remove the effect of price changes

questions.explanation: Real GDP is measured at constant prices to remove the effect of price changes.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is the GDP deflator calculated?

options.A: (Real GDP ÷ Nominal GDP) × 100

questions.explanation: GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What does GVA measure?

options.A: Total expenditure of the government
options.B: Value added by producers: output minus intermediate consumption
options.C: Total income of residents from abroad

questions.explanation: GVA measures value added by producers: output minus intermediate consumption.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is GDP at market prices related to GVA at basic prices?

options.A: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes - product subsidies
options.B: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices - product taxes + product subsidies
options.C: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes + product subsidies
options.D: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices - product taxes - product subsidies

questions.explanation: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes - product subsidies (subject to national-accounts valuation conventions).

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following does GDP NOT directly measure?

options.A: Market value of final goods and services

questions.explanation: GDP does not directly measure income distribution, unpaid work, environmental damage or quality of life.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is per-capita GDP calculated?

options.A: GDP × population

questions.explanation: Per-capita GDP = GDP ÷ population. It is an average and does not show inequality.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)?

options.A: (Employed + Unemployed persons seeking/available for work) ÷ relevant population × 100

questions.explanation: LFPR = (Employed + Unemployed persons seeking/available for work) ÷ relevant population × 100.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Worker Population Ratio (WPR)?

options.A: (Employed + Unemployed persons seeking/available for work) ÷ relevant population × 100

questions.explanation: WPR = employed persons ÷ relevant population × 100.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is the unemployment rate calculated?

options.A: Unemployed persons ÷ relevant population × 100

questions.explanation: Unemployment Rate = unemployed persons ÷ labour force × 100. It is not the unemployed share of the entire population.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is formal employment?

options.A: Jobs covered by recognised legal, tax or social-security systems
options.B: Work where a person works fewer hours than desired
options.D: Mismatch between skills and available jobs

questions.explanation: Formal employment refers to jobs covered by recognised legal, tax or social-security systems; informal work may exist inside formal or informal enterprises.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is underemployment?

options.A: Jobs covered by recognised legal, tax or social-security systems
options.B: A person works fewer hours or below their skill/capacity and wants more or better work
options.C: More workers are engaged than required
options.D: Mismatch between skills and available jobs

questions.explanation: Underemployment occurs when a person works fewer hours or below their skill/capacity and wants more or better work.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is disguised unemployment?

options.A: Jobs covered by recognised legal, tax or social-security systems
options.B: A person works fewer hours than desired
options.C: More workers are engaged than required; removing some does not materially reduce output
options.D: Mismatch between skills and available jobs

questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment occurs when more workers are engaged than required; removing some does not materially reduce output.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Structural unemployment refers to:

options.A: Temporary job search
options.C: Mismatch between skills/locations and available jobs

questions.explanation: Structural unemployment is a mismatch between skills/locations and available jobs.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Frictional unemployment refers to:

options.A: Temporary job search

questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment is temporary job search.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Cyclical unemployment refers to:

options.A: Temporary job search

questions.explanation: Cyclical unemployment is downturn-related.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is fiscal policy?

options.A: Actions by RBI to manage liquidity and interest rates
options.B: Government decisions on taxation, public expenditure and borrowing to influence aggregate demand, resource allocation, growth and distribution

questions.explanation: Fiscal policy refers to government decisions on taxation, public expenditure and borrowing to influence aggregate demand, resource allocation, growth and distribution.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is fiscal deficit calculated?

options.A: Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
options.D: Revenue deficit - Grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts). It indicates the government's borrowing requirement.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is revenue deficit calculated?

options.A: Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
options.D: Revenue deficit - Grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure - Revenue receipts. It indicates that revenue receipts are insufficient to meet revenue expenditure.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is primary deficit calculated?

options.A: Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
options.D: Revenue deficit - Grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit - Interest payments.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How is effective revenue deficit calculated?

options.A: Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
options.D: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Effective revenue deficit = Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is monetary policy?

options.A: Government decisions on taxation and expenditure
options.B: Actions by the RBI to manage liquidity, interest rates and monetary conditions in pursuit of price stability while keeping growth in mind
options.D: Management of foreign exchange reserves only

questions.explanation: Monetary policy refers to actions by the RBI to manage liquidity, interest rates and monetary conditions in pursuit of price stability while keeping growth in mind.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the repo rate?

options.A: The rate at which banks park surplus liquidity with RBI without collateral
options.B: The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to eligible banks against eligible collateral
options.C: The rate at which eligible banks borrow overnight from RBI against approved securities
options.D: The rate of return on government securities

questions.explanation: The repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to eligible banks against eligible collateral under the liquidity framework.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)?

options.A: A facility through which banks can park surplus liquidity with RBI without providing collateral
options.B: A facility allowing eligible banks to borrow overnight from RBI against approved securities
options.C: The share of NDTL banks must maintain as cash balance with RBI
options.D: The share of NDTL banks must maintain in prescribed liquid assets

questions.explanation: SDF is a facility through which banks can park surplus liquidity with RBI without providing collateral; it forms the floor of the LAF corridor.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)?

options.A: A facility through which banks can park surplus liquidity with RBI without providing collateral
options.B: A facility allowing eligible banks to borrow overnight from RBI against approved securities
options.C: The share of NDTL banks must maintain as cash balance with RBI
options.D: The share of NDTL banks must maintain in prescribed liquid assets

questions.explanation: MSF allows eligible banks to borrow overnight from RBI against approved securities, subject to conditions.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)?

options.A: The share of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities it must maintain as cash balance with RBI
options.B: The share of NDTL banks must maintain in prescribed liquid assets
options.C: The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to banks
options.D: The rate at which banks park surplus liquidity with RBI

questions.explanation: CRR is the share of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities it must maintain as cash balance with RBI.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?

options.A: The share of a bank's NDTL it must maintain as cash balance with RBI
options.B: The share of NDTL banks must maintain in prescribed liquid assets
options.C: The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to banks
options.D: The rate at which banks park surplus liquidity with RBI

questions.explanation: SLR is the share of NDTL banks must maintain in prescribed liquid assets.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What are Open Market Operations (OMOs)?

options.A: RBI purchase/sale of government securities to inject/absorb durable liquidity

questions.explanation: Open Market Operations refer to RBI purchase/sale of government securities to inject/absorb durable liquidity.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Bank Rate?

options.A: It is the same as the repo rate in all operational contexts
options.B: It is linked to specified RBI lending/penalty facilities; not the same as repo in all operational contexts
options.C: It is the rate at which banks park surplus liquidity with RBI
options.D: It is the rate of return on government securities

questions.explanation: Bank Rate is linked to specified RBI lending/penalty facilities; it is not the same as repo in all operational contexts.

questions.question: How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) have?

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Who chairs the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?

questions.explanation: The RBI Governor chairs the MPC and has a casting vote in case of a tie.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Payments Banks?

options.C: They focus only on agriculture finance

questions.question: Which institution is associated with MSME development finance?

questions.subject: Current Economy

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is an NPA (Non-Performing Asset)?

options.A: A loan classified as non-performing under RBI prudential norms; commonly, a term loan becomes NPA when interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days
options.B: A loan given to priority sectors

questions.explanation: NPA is a loan/advance classified as non-performing under RBI prudential norms; commonly, a term loan becomes NPA when interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is included in Priority Sector Lending under RBI guidelines?

options.A: Large corporate lending
options.B: Agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing and weaker sections

questions.explanation: Priority Sector Lending includes specified sectors such as agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing and weaker sections under RBI guidelines.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which institution insures eligible bank deposits in India?

options.A: RBI

questions.explanation: DICGC (Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation) insures eligible bank deposits.

options.A: ₹1 lakh

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Union Budget presented?

questions.subject: Current Economy

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax?

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is an indirect tax?

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Under which Article is the GST Council a constitutional body?

questions.explanation: GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A; it recommends GST rates, exemptions and related matters.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the GST Council?

questions.explanation: Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council; State finance/tax ministers are members.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: GST is a:

questions.explanation: GST is a destination-based, value-added indirect tax.

options.B: CPI, WPI, PLFS, UPI, forex reserves, RBI policy and market-regulator circulars
options.C: Union Budget, Karnataka Budget, Economic Survey, PLFS annual report, MSP decisions and major rankings

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: For any statistic, what should be recorded?

options.A: Value + unit + period + publication date + source + provisional/final status

questions.explanation: For any statistic, record: value + unit + period + publication date + source + provisional/final status.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: For exchange rates and forex reserves, what must always be specified?

options.A: The date/week

questions.explanation: For exchange rates and forex reserves, always specify the date/week; do not memorise an undated figure.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: For policy changes, what should be recorded?

options.A: The issuing authority, notification date, effective date and whether it is a proposal, approval or implemented measure

questions.explanation: For policy changes, record the issuing authority, notification date, effective date and whether it is a proposal, approval or implemented measure.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: What is the research cutoff of the Current Economy 1.4 material?

options.A: 30 October 2026

questions.explanation: The PDF is prepared with a research cutoff of 30 October 2026. Some fast-moving figures may have changed after the latest source publication.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the October 2026 repo-rate change?

options.A: It is flagged for confirmation against the original RBI resolution before memorising

questions.explanation: The October 2026 repo-rate change is flagged for confirmation against the original RBI resolution before memorising. The underlying RBI-hosted release was not directly retrieved in the research run.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: How should rankings be presented in exam answers?

options.A: As a study framework unless a current edition and rank were verified

questions.explanation: Rankings are presented as a study framework unless a current edition and rank were verified. This material is exam-oriented and should be cross-checked with the latest official notification before the examination.

questions.subject: Current Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct distinction between disinflation and deflation?

options.A: Disinflation is slower positive inflation; deflation is falling general price level
options.B: Disinflation is falling general price level; deflation is slower positive inflation

questions.explanation: Disinflation is slower positive inflation; deflation is falling general price level.
